Rabbiteye and Southern highbush chill requirements are known to run lower than typical Northern highbush requirements, so applying this range to V. corymbosum risks understating its real dormancy needs. soil_base — removed on audit: The cited quote ('Clay, High Organic Matter, Loam (Silt)') is NC State's Soil Texture tag list -- it describes soil composition the plant tolerates, not a growing location/medium ('garden_bed' vs. container vs. raised bed). Nothing in the quote says or implies 'garden bed.' This is a field/concept mismatch: a soil-texture citation was used to justify a soil-base (location) value it never addresses.

soil_drainage — removed on audit: The quote literally says 'Good Drainage, Moist' -- an NC State Soil Drainage tag reading 'Good,' not 'moderate.' The record silently downgrades a stated 'Good Drainage' rating to 'moderate' with no citation or reasoning bridging that gap, and also folds in a separate 'Moist' moisture tag as if it supported the drainage rating. The label doesn't survive re-derivation from its own quote.

is_houseplant — removed on audit: Both citations only establish that strawberries can be grown in outdoor pots/hanging baskets (patio containers, groundcover use) -- neither UMD nor NC State's 'Container, Hanging Baskets' tag says or implies indoor houseplant cultivation. This is reinforced by internal inconsistency: the record's own outdoor_sun_exposure requires 6+ hours of direct sunlight (full_sun) with no light_fc/humidity data populated for indoor conditions, which is inconsistent with true houseplant status. Container-capable outdoors is not the same claim as 'is_houseplant.'

chill_damage_f — removed on audit: The UGA quote states a threshold for open BLOSSOMS specifically ('strawberry blossoms don't freeze until 28 degrees') during spring bloom, not a general whole-plant cold-damage floor. Dormant strawberry crowns are considerably more cold-hardy than open flowers; collapsing a bloom-stage, flower-specific frost point into a general chill_damage_f field risks misapplying it outside the bloom window (e.g., implying the whole plant is damaged at 28°F when only exposed blossoms are at that specific risk). The number (28) is accurately quoted, but the scope of what it measures is narrower than what the field name implies.

name_note — removed on audit: The note asserts a specific factual claim -- 'Per Clemson HGIC, the species arose as a hybrid cross of Fragaria virginiana ... and Fragaria chiloensis' -- that is attributed to a named source but has no corresponding entry in the citations array (no URL, no quote). None of the actual Clemson HGIC citations in the record mention virginiana or chiloensis. This is an unverifiable, uncited assertion smuggled into a supposedly source-grounded field.

Only the NC State Plant Toolbox page (anchor) carried a structured Dimensions/Edibility/Attracts block; searched Clemson HGIC, UMD Extension, and the UGA CAES field report for size, edibility, and pollinator language and found none relevant to this species (Clemson's only 'Poison'/'Toxic' hits were an unrelated 'Poison Ivy' related-post link, not content about strawberry).
